findings.title: A bounded field of responsibility
findings.claim: The control verb joined to Moses's self and brother names a bounded field of personal responsibility, after which the prayer places that pair on a distinct side from the boundary-breaking collective.
findings.mechanism: The focus possession-and-disposal carrier meets the exceptive frame and its two named objects; the living-person sense of nafsi and the paired brother relation make the accountable unit concrete, while the repeated between-frame under the separation imperative makes the boundary relational and visible. The supplied wider parallels return this same distinction through personal accountability, the Moses-Harun pair, and a direct separation request.
findings.reader_payoff: The request becomes newly perceptible as a precise allocation of answerability rather than a general dismissal of a people.
findings.containment: The plain request to separate Moses and his brother from the qawm al-fasiqin remains intact. This reading bounds responsibility; it does not declare the collective innocent or claim that Moses has no authority at all.
